title: Valid Parentheses
statement: A string contains only the brackets ( ) [ ] and { }. Decide whether it is well formed: every opening bracket is closed by the same kind of bracket, and pairs nest properly without crossing.

example.caption: Each closer meets the most recent unclosed opener. Everything pairs up, so the answer is true.

idea.sentence: The last opener you saw must be the first one to close. A stack gives exactly that order.

jargon.plain: A pile where you only add or remove at the top: last in, first out.

watch.inputHint: One argument: a string of brackets, e.g. "([]{})"

compare.bruteLabel: Delete matching pairs again and again

rows.name: Brute force
rows.note: Repeatedly remove adjacent pairs like () until nothing changes. Each sweep costs n and there can be n/2 sweeps.

rows.name: Stack
rows.note: Each character is pushed once and popped at most once. The stack can hold all n if they are all openers.

fast.takeaway: A stack remembers openers in the exact order they need to close. That removes the repeated rescanning.

stages.title: Pairs and stack
stages.note: A lookup from each closer to its opener, and an empty stack for openers still waiting.

stages.title: Push openers
stages.note: An opener has no partner yet. Push it on the stack.

stages.title: Match closers
stages.note: Pop the top. It must be the opener for this closer. Empty stack or wrong kind means invalid.

stages.title: Stack empty?
stages.note: Leftover openers were never closed. Valid only if the stack is empty.

edges.title: Empty string
edges.why: Nothing is open, so nothing is wrong. The stack ends empty.

edges.title: Only an opener
edges.why: It is pushed and never closed. The final empty check catches it.

edges.title: Closer first
edges.why: Popping an empty stack must count as a mismatch, not a crash.

edges.title: Crossed pairs
edges.why: Counts balance, but the order is wrong. ) meets [ on top, not (.

gotchas.text: stack.pop() on an empty array returns undefined. Compared with an opener it is simply not equal, so a lone closer fails correctly. Do not add a ! assertion.
stack[len(stack)-1] on an empty slice panics. Check len(stack) == 0 first.
Indexing a string gives a byte, ranging over it gives a rune. For ASCII brackets bytes are fine.
Counting brackets of each kind is not enough. "([)]" has balanced counts but is invalid.
Forgetting the final empty check wrongly accepts "(((".

recap.key: Push openers. Each closer must match the top of the stack. At the end the stack must be empty.
moves: Map each closer to its opener
On a closer, pop and compare. Mismatch or empty means false
Return whether the stack is empty
